answer: Sybil resistance follows when trust propagates through bounded-length random walks on an attestation graph: a cluster with few links to honest participants has low conductance, so little walk probability crosses its boundary. Spectral expansion and min-cut transitivity bounds then limit the cluster’s reachable trust mass, and thus its aggregate voting weight, relative to honest seed mass; labels such as nebula, ivory, and quartz do not alter that cut-based bound.
